topics.title: Configuring Work Groups and Work Queues

elements.description: Organization, division and unit describe the enterprise hierarchy; units can have children. Work groups represent operational teams that can span business units. These records support routing and reporting but do not replace access roles.

elements.text: Worked example: A retailer has an organization, regional divisions and fulfillment units. A returns work group spans fulfillment and support without changing the reporting hierarchy.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Configuring Work Groups and Work Queues

elements.description: A work queue holds shared assignments; a work group associates operators, managers and queues. A worklist holds assignments for an individual operator. Match team-level routing to a queue and individual ownership to a worklist.

elements.text: Worked example: Route unclaimed returns reviews to ReturnsQueue, then let eligible operators obtain work. A named specialist's follow-up can go to that specialist's worklist.

items.label: Configuring Work Groups and Work Queues

elements.description: Maintain operator organizational membership, work group/queue associations and routing references together. Test that eligible team members can retrieve shared work and that managers can oversee the intended group; renaming an organization is not a substitute for updating routing.

elements.text: Worked example: When a new branch opens, create its unit and operators, associate them with the appropriate work group, and test queue access and escalation to the manager.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Hierarchy versus team
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Every work group must be a division.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use work groups for operational collaboration across units.

examPitfalls.title: Queue versus list
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A work queue belongs to one individual like a worklist.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A queue contains shared work; a worklist represents individual assignments.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which order describes the standard organization hierarchy?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Organization records model the enterprise as organization, division and unit, with possible child units.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Designers and analysts in different units collaborate on shared work. Which record models their operational team?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A work group can span organizational units and associates the operational team with shared queues and management.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An unassigned task must be available to several eligible team members. Where should it be routed?

options.text: A clipboard-only list with no assignment
One operator's personal worklist regardless of availability

practiceQuiz.rationale: A work queue holds shared assignments. A personal worklist would give the task individual ownership.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A task is explicitly assigned to one specialist. Which container represents that person's assignments?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A worklist holds assignments for an individual operator; work queues hold shared work.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO belong to work group configuration concerns?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A work group connects team members, management and shared queues. Database tuning and package integrity are separate concerns.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An operator moves to a new team but sees no shared tasks. Which configuration should be checked first?

options.text: Operator work group and queue associations

practiceQuiz.rationale: Membership and queue associations determine the operational work available to the operator. Visual settings do not route work.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new unit is created. Which test best validates the accompanying routing change?

options.text: Create a case and verify its assignment reaches the intended queue or operator
Check only that the unit label renders

practiceQuiz.rationale: The actual assignment destination validates routing. A visible organizational record does not prove the routing references are correct.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Does placing an operator in a division alone establish all application permissions?

options.text: Only if the work queue is empty
No; access groups, roles and policies still govern authorization
Yes; every division grants full developer access

practiceQuiz.rationale: Organization membership can inform routing and authorization logic, but it is not a universal replacement for access-control configuration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
